name: Alexander the Great
hook: A Macedonian king who cut the Gordian knot, crushed Persia by 30, and died with nowhere left to conquer.

facts.label: Pella
facts.statement: Alexander was born in Pella, the Macedonian capital, in a region that is now part of Greece.

facts.label: Aristotle
facts.statement: Aristotle was hired by Philip II to tutor Alexander; he later wrote the Constitution of Athens.

facts.label: Philip II of Macedon
facts.statement: Philip II, Alexander's father, was assassinated at a wedding in 336 B.C. by Pausanias; Alexander succeeded him.

facts.label: the Gordian knot
facts.statement: Alexander solved the Gordian knot by cutting it with his sword, after hearing only the future ruler of Asia could untie it.

facts.label: Darius III
facts.statement: Alexander defeated Darius III at Gaugamela in 331 B.C.; the last Achaemenid king of Persia was later killed by one of his own men.

facts.label: India
facts.statement: Alexander led his army as far east as the Hyphasis River, now the Beas, in India.

facts.label: Ptolemy
facts.statement: Ptolemy, once a bodyguard of Alexander, took Egypt after Alexander's death and founded a dynasty that lasted until Cleopatra.
